title: Conditions: if, else, switch
idea: A condition picks which code runs: JavaScript evaluates an expression, treats the result as true or false, and runs exactly one branch.

analogy.text: A fork in the road with a sign on each path. You read the sign, then take exactly one path.
analogy.breaks: A fork has fixed signs; a condition is re-evaluated every time the code runs.

points: `if` runs its block when the condition is truthy; `else` covers everything else.
In an `else if` chain the first true test wins; the rest are skipped.
`switch` compares one value against many `case` labels using `===`.

hero.title: What counts as false
hero.verdict: Everything that is not on the falsy list is truthy.

code.title: if and switch
code.caption: An `else if` chain picks one branch. Two `case` labels in a row share one block.

challenges.intro: Write each function, run the tests, and open a hint only when you are stuck.

items.title: Even or odd
hints: The remainder operator `%` gives what is left after a division.
An even number leaves remainder 0 when divided by 2.
Test `n % 2 === 0`, and `return` the right word in each branch.

items.title: Letter grade
items.prompt: Write `grade(score)`: 90 and up is `"A"`, 80 and up `"B"`, 70 and up `"C"`, anything lower `"F"`.
hints: A test only runs if the ones above it failed, so `score >= 80` already means below 90.
End with a plain `return 'F'` for everything left.

items.title: Leap year
items.prompt: Write `isLeapYear(year)`. A leap year divides by 4, except century years, which must divide by 400.
hints: Split the rule in two: the usual leap years, then the century exception.
Divisible by 4 and not by 100 is one way to be a leap year.
The other way is divisible by 400. Join the two ways with `||`.

items.title: Fizz, Buzz or FizzBuzz
items.prompt: Write `fizzbuzz(n)`: `"FizzBuzz"` if `n` divides by 3 and 5, `"Fizz"` by 3, `"Buzz"` by 5, otherwise `n` itself.
hints: Order matters: one number can match several tests.
A number divisible by both 3 and 5 is divisible by 15. Test that case first.
Return the number itself when nothing matches.

items.title: Weekday or weekend
items.prompt: Write `dayType(day)` with a `switch`: `"sat"` and `"sun"` give `"weekend"`, `"mon"` to `"fri"` give `"weekday"`, anything else `"unknown"`.
hints: Stack several `case` labels with no code between them to share one result.
A `return` inside a case also leaves the `switch`, so no `break` is needed.
Put `default:` last for everything you did not list.

pitfalls: Use `===`, not `==`: loose equality converts types and surprises you.
A `case` without `break` or `return` falls through into the next case.
Put the most specific test first; a broader test above it hides it.

quiz.why: `0` is falsy, so the first test fails. The second test is true, and the chain stops there.

takeaway: Conditions pick one branch; order your tests from most specific to most general.

starters: Why is an empty array truthy but an empty string falsy?
When should I use switch instead of else if?
What is the difference between == and ===?
